transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-23
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Omar (Redwood Product), Alex (Polaris Head of ML), Maya (Infra), Priya (Data Platform)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood's model curation checklist and the compatibility matrix in the Console and Optimize tool. Focused on how Polaris can shortlist open models for their summarization and analytics pipelines, run lightweight benchmarks, and map model variants to runtime profiles for hosted vs dedicated deployments. Discussed security posture (VPC, KMS), and a pilot plan.

Topics covered:
- Model shortlisting checklist (quality, latency, token cost, quantization)
- Console: compatibility matrix and kernel mapping view
- Optimize: bench harness integration and recommended batching/quantization profiles
- Hosting options and fallback routing policies
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, VPC

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): All right everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — from Redwood we have Jenna and Omar, and from Polaris Alex, Maya and Priya. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Alex (Polaris): Good, thanks. Excited to see the curation checklist — we've been trying to formalize our model selection process rather than ad hoc picks.
[00:20] Jenna (Redwood SE): Great. The aim today is to show the Console flow for shortlisting open models, then jump into Optimize where you can run bench runs and get suggested quantization and batching. We'll also point out the compatibility matrix that maps models to kernels and hardware.
[00:35] Maya (Polaris): Quick practical note — our infra team cares a lot about memory profiles and KV cache behavior, because we plan to run long-context summarizations.
[00:45] Jenna: Yep that's on the checklist — we capture memory, peak GPU memory, kv-cache growth per token, and typical sequence length distribution.
[00:52] Priya (Polaris): Also curious how the catalog handles custom finetuned variants. We have a few lightly fine-tuned checkpoints.
[00:58] Omar (Redwood Product): We treat finetuned variants as catalog siblings. In the Console you can pin variants, and in routing you can say prefer finetuned for certain routes with fallback to base model.
[01:08] Alex: Nice. Can we see an example?
[01:12] Jenna: Sure — pulling up the Console. (short pause) Okay, here's the model shortlist UI. On the left you see filters: license (open, redistributable), token cost estimate, latency band, typical where it fits (chat vs summarization), and quantization friendliness.
[01:30] Samir: A lot of customers like the 'compatibility score' we compute. It's a heuristic: hardware match + kernel maturity + observed bench stability. It's meant to prioritize models to try first.
[01:42] Alex: I like the idea, how noisy is that score? We've seen mismatches before.
[01:46] Jenna: It's intentionally conservative. We show the components so you can override — e.g., if kernel maturity is low but you have capacity to test, you can still flag the model.
[01:55] Maya: On kernel maturity, our stack is Ampere A800 and a couple of H100s in cloud. How do we know which kernels will be used for a particular model?
[02:05] Jenna: In the compatibility matrix view you can expand a model and see kernel mappings per backend — e.g., Triton kernel X for H100, CUDA-fused kernel Y for A800. There's also a note for recommended quantization levels and any known regression risks.
[02:18] Alex: Do you expose perf deltas for 8-bit vs 4-bit?
[02:22] Omar: Yes — Optimize runs bench jobs and reports latency/throughput and a quality delta metric against your reference prompt set. It recommends a quantization profile that balances the two.
[02:32] Samir: Quick interruption — many teams trade off latency vs cost. We also provide 'routing policies' where you can route high priority traffic to non-quantized or dedicated pool, and fallback lower priority to quantized variants for cost savings.
[02:46] Priya: That sounds useful. For our summarization use-case, we have a strict SLA for enterprise customers: 200ms p95 on short requests, and 1.5s p95 for long sessions.
[02:57] Jenna: We can map those SLOs to model profiles. In the Console you can tag a model as 'low latency' if it meets your p95 under the target hardware and batch size.
[03:10] Alex: Show us a bench run?
[03:12] Jenna: Yep — switching to Optimize. Here is a bench run we ran earlier for a 7b open model on A800. You can see time-series of latency, token/sec, and model quality on the evals we uploaded.
[03:25] Maya: The latency graph looks spiky — is that jitter from autoscaling?
[03:28] Jenna: Could be. In this run we used mixed workload. Optimize annotates when GPU packing changed or when KV cache misses occurred. Sometimes a cold KV cache causes a first-token spike.
[03:38] Speaker 1: (inaudible) first-token problem.
[03:41] Samir: Also worth noting, we do prefix caching and you can enable persistent KV for sessions which reduces those spikes significantly for conversational workloads.
[03:49] Alex: About benchmarks — we want to run bench runs that mimic production traffic. What's needed from our side?
[03:55] Jenna: Ideally, a representative prompt set, along with the token mix and concurrency. We have a bench harness (we'll share the script). You can run it in your environment or in the Redwood trial org.
[04:06] Alex: We'd prefer to run in our private deployment first — don't want tokens leaving our VPC.
[04:10] Omar: No problem. For Private deployments we provide the same Console and Optimize tooling via the private control plane. Bench data can be stored on-prem or in your cloud account.
[04:20] Maya: On security: we need SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML support, and KMS integration. Also audit logs that show model and route changes.
[04:28] Samir: We'll send the SOC2 report and our KMS integration guide — we've done HSM integrations as well. The Console emits audit logs for model pins, rollout changes, and routing edits.
[04:38] Priya: About data retention — can we configure logs retention to meet our compliance?
[04:42] Omar: Yes, retention is configurable for Dedicated and Private; hosted orgs have tiers. We'll include that in the security doc pack.
[04:50] Alex: Back to model selection — the curation checklist you mentioned earlier, can you walk through the steps you recommend?
[04:55] Jenna: Absolutely. Our curation checklist has five phases: 1) discovery & license check (ensure redistributable if you need to ship weights), 2) shortlisting by quality/benchmark seeds, 3) runtime fit (memory, kv-cache, quantization friendliness), 4) pilot in dedicated or private with routing/fallback rules, 5) rollout with monitoring and quality regressions gated by evals.
[05:15] Alex: For step 2, can Optimize run our evals out of the box?
[05:18] Jenna: Yes — you can upload eval prompt sets. We run quality metrics (exact-match, rouge, and custom scoring functions) and show regressions vs a baseline model.
[05:26] Maya: Do you support custom scoring scripts? We have a post-processing step for our transcripts.
[05:30] Jenna: You can add a scoring hook. For private deployments, the hook runs inside your environment; for hosted we run it in a sandboxed environment.
[05:38] Alex: Any gotchas with finetuned models and kernel mapping?
[05:41] Omar: Sometimes finetuned weights change tokenizer or special tokens. That can affect caching heuristics. We recommend running a small sanity bench to validate tokenization and effective sequence length. The Console flags tokenization mismatches.
[05:54] Priya: What's the best way to reduce token cost without large quality drop?
[05:58] Samir: Common levers — prompt engineering, prefix caching, and selective quantization for lower-prio routes. Optimize will suggest a quantization profile and estimate quality delta.
[06:10] Alex: Can you demo a compatibility matrix export? We want to share with our infra team.
[06:14] Jenna: Sure — exporting now. (pause) Here's the CSV: rows are models, columns are hardware types, quantization options, kernel maturity, and an estimated TCO per million tokens. I'll share the link after the call.
[06:28] Maya: Nice. How accurate is the TCO number?
[06:30] Omar: It's an estimate based on observed tokens/sec and instance pricing. For Dedicated customers you can plug in committed pricing and it will recalc.
[06:38] Alex: About pilot scope — timeline-wise we want to pick two model candidates, run bench, and decide within 3 weeks. Is that feasible?
[06:45] Jenna: That's tight but doable. If Polaris provides prompt sets and traffic profile in the next 3 business days we can schedule bench runs and have results within a week.
[06:55] Maya: We'll sync offline to get you the data.
[07:00] Priya: One more question: how do you handle rollout rollback in the Console if a model shows regression?
[07:06] Omar: We support canary rollouts and automatic rollback rules based on eval metrics or latency SLO violations. You can set thresholds and we will revert traffic to the previous variant if exceeded.
[07:18] Alex: Good. Any limitations for long-context models? We've been experimenting with 32k context windows.
[07:24] Jenna: Long-context affects kernel selection and memory footprint. The runtime picks specialized kernels for chunked attention where available, but some open models still lack optimized kernels and will fall back to generic paths — that increases latency. It's on the compatibility matrix.
[07:38] Speaker 2: (background) yep
[07:40] Samir: If you'd like, we can run a targeted long-context bench on H100 with your longest prompts to show real numbers.
[07:47] Alex: Let's do that as part of the pilot.
[07:50] Jenna: Great — action: we'll provision a trial project and upload the bench harness. Also we'll share the curation checklist doc and security pack.
[07:58] Priya: How do we invite our infra folks to the trial org?
[08:02] Samir: I'll send an invite link. For private deployment trials we do a lightweight onboarding call with infra.
[08:10] Alex: Any other integration concerns — CI/CD ties, model versioning?
[08:14] Omar: The Console integrates with your model registry via webhooks and supports tagging versions. You can trigger bench runs on PRs or when a new variant is pushed.
[08:24] Maya: That's important for our ML platform.
[08:26] Speaker 1: (muffled)
[08:28] Samir: Okay wrapping up, recap of next steps — we'll send pricing and TCO, provide trial org and bench harness, and share security docs. Polaris will send prompt sets and traffic profile.
[08:41] Alex: Sounds good. Anything on contracts or procurement?
[08:44] Samir: We'll include a starter procurement checklist in the email. For Dedicated we can give a 90-day pilot with a short-term credit.
[08:52] Priya: Thanks. One final ask — can you include an example rollout runbook? Our SREs like step-by-step.
[08:58] Jenna: Yes, we'll attach a runbook template.
[09:02] Alex: Great, that's it from us.
[09:05] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and next steps.
[55:30] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional speaker mislabels and brief audio drop caused a few words to be unclear (marked inaudible).
